blocks.text: Known 55+ manufactured-home parks and co-ops: what the sources show
Westwood Court — 8670 156 St (Fleetwood Tynehead, Fleetwood)

A gated manufactured-home park. Current listings describe "one of Fleetwood's most desirable 55+ communities" and a "Gated 55+ community close to shopping, restaurants, Fresh St. Market, Fleetwood Sport & Leisure Centre, library, medical services, and transit," with the pad fee including water, garbage and management, and pets welcome. Listing-stated — confirm the age rule, pad rent and pet rules against the park's tenancy agreement and park rules.
Westwood Estates — 134 St, Newton (Queen Mary Park Surrey filing)

A gated manufactured-home park. Current listings describe "WESTWOOD ESTATES, 55+ age restricted: Located in one of Surrey's most premier, sought after manufactured home parks, gated community," with a clubhouse, pad rent in the listings checked including the land portion of property taxes, garbage pickup, sewer and water, and large dogs allowed with park approval but no vicious breeds (MLS®; MLS®). Address note: current listings use both 8224 134 Street and 8254 134 Street as the park address — confirm the civic address and pad number from the park office. Sources differ: listings checked state different pad rents for different units and dates ($822/mo, $912.52/mo stated for Jan 1, 2027, $915/mo and $935/mo) — do not publish any one of them as "the" park rate; confirm the current figure for the specific pad in the tenancy agreement.
Good to know before you buy a park home

items.t: The three park entries in rest on current MLS listing text and a park directory that name the park and state its age rule — solid enough to print as listing-stated, not a substitute for the park's own rules document.

Two Surrey parks share almost the same name, in two different communities. Westwood Court is the Fleetwood park at 8670 156 Street; Westwood Estates is the Newton park on 134 Street, whose own listings disagree on 8224 vs 8254 as the civic address. An alert set on one name does not cover the other park, and a showing booked off the wrong 134 Street address is a wasted trip.

Aggregator data mislabels a park's pad fee as a strata fee. A current Westwood Court listing's data fields record the monthly park charge under "Strata Fees" — a park home has no strata fee; that figure is the pad fee the listing text describes as including water, garbage and management. Read the listing text, not the aggregator's field label, before comparing a park home's carrying costs against a condo's.

One of Surrey's four 55+ manufactured-home communities is not a park at all, and the clue is in its listings. Sea Ridge Bays' listings say "Council Approval Required" and record title as Freehold Strata — it is a bare-land strata on 20 Avenue in South Surrey, so its buyers get strata documents and a Form B, not a tenancy agreement and park rules, and its 55+ rule is a strata bylaw with provincial exemptions a park does not offer.

The city's zoning has a park-specific zone, and a separate mobile-homes bylaw. Zone RM-M, Manufactured Home Residential Zone (Surrey Zoning By-law, 1993, No. 12000, Part 19), is the dedicated zone for this housing form, and the City's regulatory-bylaw list separately carries Bylaw No. 6142, "Mobile Homes & Trailer" — a park's zoning and bylaw position, not just its rules, is part of its long-term security.

The two King George Boulevard parks nearest the Newton parks are not seniors parks. Crispen Bays (7790 King George Blvd) and Crestway Bays (8220 King George Blvd) are listed by a park directory as all-ages, and Crestway listings call the park family-oriented — a buyer who assumes every Newton-corridor park is seniors-only will be wrong on these two, minutes from the genuinely 55+ Newton Mobile Home Park at 6571.

The Fleetwood park's transit story changes on a dated provincial project. Westwood Court's listings already market the "future SkyTrain" — the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain extension along Fraser Highway, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029, is the project that changes Fleetwood's transit position; today SkyTrain serves only City Centre / Whalley in Surrey.

blocks.text: Surrey Mobile Homes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Westwood Court, 8670 156 Street, sits in Fleetwood east of 156 Street's Fraser Highway corridor; Westwood Estates, on 134 Street (listings use both 8224 and 8254 — confirm the civic address), sits in Queen Mary Park west of King George Boulevard.

Newton Mobile Home Park (Newton MHP), 6571 King George Boulevard, and Crispen Bays, 7790 King George Boulevard, and Crestway Bays, 8220 King George Boulevard, form a King George Boulevard strip in Newton; Sea Ridge Bays, 15875 20 Avenue, is the South Surrey outlier, south toward the Nicomekl lowlands.

blocks.text: Surrey Mobile Homes: the housing stock

items.t: Crispen Bays, 7790 King George Boulevard, and Crestway Bays, 8220 King George Boulevard: pad-rental tenure records only, carried as all-ages — never known stock.
Sea Ridge Bays, 15875 20 Avenue: bare-land strata, carried as 55+ — the buyer owns the strata lot, so it is not a pad tenancy at all.
Tenure line, for every Surrey pad park above: a home on a rented pad is not land ownership — the buyer owns the home as a chattel and rents the pad under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement.

blocks.text: Surrey Mobile Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Surrey regulates manufactured home parks through Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 — check the park's zone and the bylaw's manufactured-home-park provisions for the specific address before relying on continued park use.

Surrey's Manufactured Home Park Redevelopment and Strata Conversion Policy O-34A adds a City layer on top of provincial law when a Surrey park is redeveloped or strata-converted: the City brochure states the owner must notify residents of the application and the Council meeting, and the policy addresses relocation of existing residents and a right of first refusal to purchase.

Surrey Tenant Protection Bylaw No. 21788 (2025) does not cover these homes: the City states it does not apply to property governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act — Surrey pad tenants rely on the provincial Act plus Policy O-34A, not Bylaw 21788.

blocks.text: Surrey Mobile Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Two Surrey parks differ by one word and sit in two different communities: Westwood COURT is Fleetwood (8670 156 Street) and Westwood ESTATES is Queen Mary Park (134 Street) — an alert or a park-rule request sent to the wrong one diligence-checks the wrong park.

Surrey school catchments are address-based in School District No. 36 (Surrey): the district states your catchment school is set by your address on its School Boundaries Map and directs families to its School Locator tool; confirm the school for a specific park address with the locator, because no named school is promised for any Surrey park.

South Surrey's Sea Ridge Bays pocket at 15875 20 Avenue sits in the low ground south of the Nicomekl River system: Surrey's lowlands there are diked and drained by pump stations under the Serpentine–Nicomekl lowlands flood control works, a different flood setting from the raised Newton and Fleetwood park sites — check the specific lot, not the city.

Surrey bills utilities two ways: a property without a water meter pays an annual flat rate once a year, and a metered property is billed every 4 months — which system a park passes through to residents is a park-documents question, not stated on the City page for any named park.

A Surrey park home has no strata fee even when a listing form labels its monthly park charge that way — the charge is pad rent under a site tenancy, and the RTB, not a strata council, is the dispute route.

A Surrey manufactured home cannot be sold without its original legible CSA (Canadian Standards Association) certification label — Z-240 for a mobile home, A-277 for a modular home — and a lost label needs Technical Safety BC re-certification before a sale can register.

blocks.text: Surrey Mobile Homes: development and new projects

items.t: Surrey Rental Replacement Policy No. O-63 and Tenant Protection Bylaw No. 21788 were both adopted October 20, 2025 for multi-unit rental redevelopment — status: in force when read on 2026-11-03; neither applies to manufactured home park property, which stays under Policy O-34A and provincial law.

blocks.text: Surrey Mobile Homes: costs and taxes

items.t: City of Surrey 2026 residential (Class 1) property tax: $3.42731 per $1,000 of assessed value in total, of which the City's own municipal total is $1.84251 per $1,000 (general municipal $1.68947 plus roads and traffic $0.15304), with school, TransLink, Metro Vancouver, BC Assessment and Municipal Finance Authority levies making up the rest.

Surrey 2026 annual flat-rate water and sewer for a single-family dwelling is $1,195 water plus $1,661 sewer, $2,856 in total; metered water is $1.4116 per cubic metre and metered sewer $2.3593 per cubic metre in 2026 — these are City dwelling rates, and a park's own billing to pad tenants is set by the park, not this table.
BC Assessment treatment: a manufactured home in a Surrey park is assessed on the home only, excluding the park land value, because the land is owned by someone other than the home owner.

The Speculation and Vacancy Tax applies in the City of Surrey: the Province lists the City of Surrey as a designated taxable area, and only owners of residential-class property there must complete the annual declaration.

blocks.text: Surrey Mobile Homes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood check for the South Surrey pocket: Surrey City Policy O-55, Development within the Nicomekl and Serpentine River Floodplains (adopted 2008), regulates development and filling in the 200-year floodplain, and City minutes record proposals inside the Serpentine 200-year floodplain being tested against O-55 — look up the Sea Ridge Bays lot's floodplain position with the City; the policy tells you the development rules, not whether a specific home has flooded.

Park-status check: confirm a Surrey park's zoning in Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 and ask the City whether any Policy O-34A redevelopment or strata-conversion application is active for that address — zoning alone does not tell you a park owner's intentions.

Manufactured Home Registry check: a sale, transfer or purchase of a manufactured home is effective only if registered in the provincial Manufactured Home Registry, filed through a lawyer or notary with the original signed Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership — the Registry confirms the home's ownership record, not the pad tenancy's park-rule position.

faq.a: Three pad-rent parks verify: Westwood Court (8670 156 St, Fleetwood), Westwood Estates (134 St, Newton — listings use both 8224 and 8254) and Newton Mobile Home Park (6571 King George Blvd, West Newton, 34 sites) — each on current listing or directory text that names the park and states the 55+ age restriction. A fourth manufactured-home option, Sea Ridge Bays (15875 20 Ave, South Surrey), is 55+ but is a bare-land strata, not a park.

Pad rent is the big one, and it is park-specific and listing-stated only: Westwood Court's listings state the pad fee includes water, garbage and management; Westwood Estates' listings state pad rent including the land portion of property taxes, garbage pickup, sewer and water. Confirm the current figure for the specific pad in the tenancy agreement — pad rent is not a strata fee and is not set by the seller.
faq.q: What are the carrying costs on top of the purchase?

faq.a: Park by park, and all three parks allow some: Westwood Court's listings state pets welcome; Westwood Estates allows large dogs with park approval, no vicious breeds; Newton Mobile Home Park listings state one pet allowed, subject to park rules; Sea Ridge Bays listings state two dogs with no size restrictions. Confirm in the park rules or strata bylaws for the specific community before writing.

Surrey adds a City layer to the provincial Act: under the City's Manufactured Home Park Policy the property owner must give 12 months' notice of a final moving date, can only give it after receiving all permits and approvals, and must pay $20,000 on or before the move-out date. Surrey's 2025 Tenant Protection Bylaw does not cover park residents — it expressly does not apply to property governed by the MHPTA.
faq.q: What happens if a park is redeveloped?

faq.a: Establish the tenure before anything else: the paperwork, financing and monthly costs are different for each.
faq.q: Do all Surrey "mobile homes" sit on rented pads?

faq.a: Two layers, and neither is Surrey's Tenant Protection Bylaw, which excludes manufactured home park property. Provincially, closure needs all permits in place, 12 months' notice and $20,000 compensation; in Surrey, Policy O-34A also requires the owner to notify residents of the application and Council meeting and addresses relocation and first refusal to purchase.
faq.q: If a Surrey park is sold for redevelopment, what protects me?

faq.a: Get the park rules and the written tenancy agreement from the seller before asking.
faq.q: Does buying the home transfer the pad to me automatically?

faq.a: No. Sea Ridge Bays, 15875 20 Avenue, is bare-land strata — you own the home and the strata lot, and strata law governs. Westwood Court, 8670 156 Street, is a rented pad — you own only the home as a chattel. The two Surrey forms have different taxes, different sale paperwork and different protection on closure, so never compare them on price alone.
faq.q: Is Sea Ridge Bays in South Surrey the same kind of purchase as Westwood Court?

faq.a: No. The Province states a manufactured home is assessed and taxed like other residential property, but the assessed value does not include the land value where the home sits in a manufactured home park on land owned by someone else. A principal-residence home can still qualify for the Home Owner Grant, applied for each year.
faq.q: Do I pay property tax on the land under a Surrey park home?
